title: Challenge: Median of Medians

writing.exampleCaption: Complete std-only median-of-medians program for its typed teaching fixture. Parsing and output construction are separate from the core algorithm.
writing.explanation:
Median grouping guarantees a constant fraction can be discarded. The worked program demonstrates this invariant on an independent fixture, so you can study the implementation before predicting the challenge result.

For teaching input `[9,8,7,6,5]`, the worked program returns `9`. Its functions are complete and use only std. Adapt the same state transitions to the visible challenge input `[12,3,5,7,4,19,26,1,9]`; predict that result before opening the answer reveal. The precise contract is: Return the fifth smallest value using deterministic selection.

Return canonical output: lowercase booleans, decimal integers without leading zeros, comma-separated values and semicolon-separated groups, with no extra whitespace or final newline. Whole medians use integer form and half medians use .5. Textual sentinels such as none and # retain their stated meaning. String and character-grid fixtures use ASCII unless the lesson explicitly specifies Unicode scalar values.

Solve the exact task, not just the visible example: Return the fifth smallest value using deterministic selection. On input `[12,3,5,7,4,19,26,1,9]`, predict the output before opening the answer reveal. The revealed output is a test oracle for this case, while private checks exercise other legal cases. Start by stating the input grammar and output format in your own words. Parse the complete input, including surrounding whitespace, before relying on any convenient positions in the example.

Build the solution around one maintained claim: Choose a guaranteed-good pivot from medians of small groups before selecting one side. Decide what state represents that claim, how it is initialized, what a single update does, and when the algorithm stops. Sorting establishes global order; selection asks only for a rank or partition. Explain which comparisons make progress toward that goal. Trace the visible input by hand and record at least two intermediate states, not only the final answer. If the trace cannot justify your predicted output, there is a gap between the idea and the implementation.

Check both correctness and cost. The intended bound is O(n) worst-case time · O(n) or in-place variants; explain which operation dominates it and how many times the input can trigger that operation. Test all-equal keys, already ordered input, reverse order, and extreme pivot or bucket distributions. Add one small case that should succeed, one boundary case, and one case chosen to challenge the invariant. Compare your hand result with the program's result, then use a failing case to fix the earliest incorrect state transition rather than patching the final output.
writing.feedback: For this input the result is `6`. Median grouping guarantees a constant fraction can be discarded. Compare this independent fixture with the worked trace: Groups of up to five are sorted locally. Recursively select a median of those group medians, then partition around it. For [12,3,5,7,4,19,26,1,9], the fifth smallest is 7; no full global sort is needed for selection.
